articles.title: Major Shonen Jump Anime Confirms Season 2 Return After Manga Finale (First Look Revealed)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha A major Shonen Jump series has officially released its final chapter after five years, and now it's confirmed the anime's return for its second season after the manga's grand finale. Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch first announced it was going to be ending with its final chapter last week, and now that's indeed come to pass […]
articles.content:
Witch Watch wrapped up the TV anime's debut season last year after a successful first outing. It was such a hit that the franchise quickly confirmed that Season 2 would be in the works, but not much had been revealed about the new season at the time. But with the end of the manga this week, Witch Watch Season 2 has released its first look as it gears up for its debut next year. You can check it out below.

Now that Witch Watch has officially ended with Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine after a five year run , Witch Watch has confirmed that Season 2 of the anime will be making its debut on screens sometime next year. No release date or window has been announced as of this time, nor have any details about potential returning production staff or cast neither. It's still a rather mysterious production, but with a 2027 return set it won't be too much longer before the anime starts to reveal more about what to expect from its return.

Witch Watch' s debut season was directed by Hiroshi Ikehata and Masao Kawase for Bibury Animation Studios with Deko Akao handling the scripts, Haruko Iizuka handling the character designs, Mutsumi Takemiya editing the anime, and Yukari Hashimoto composing the music. There's a hope that the production staff will be returning for their respective roles given how well received that first season was last year , but the voice cast is ready for their new season coming our way.

“Congratulations on the completion of the original work!” Nico voice star Rina Kawaguchi stated in a special message to Witch Watch creator Kenta Shinohara on the anime's official website . “Thank you for the wonderful story! I truly love both the comedic episodes, which are full of Shinohara-sensei's signature style and make viewers happy, and the serious episodes that really tighten things up.” But although the star is saying goodbye to the series, there's a hope she returns in the anime's future.

If you wanted to catch up on Witch Watch ahead of the second season, you can now find its episodes now streaming with platforms such as Netflix, Hulu and Hulu on Disney+, Crunchyroll and more in the meantime with both Japanese and English language audio. You can also check out the manga's final chapter completely for free with Shueisha's MangaPlus service or Viz Media's digital Shonen Jump library. And given its wacky adventures and intense action, you're going to want to.

Are you excited to see Witch Watch return for a new season? What are you hoping to see from the new episodes? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda Insider Gives New Update on Majora's Mask Remake
articles.summary: A Nintendo insider has given a new update on the rumored remake of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask. Before Breath of the Wild came along, Majora's Mask was commonly viewed as the second greatest Legend of Zelda game of all time, behind only Ocarina of Time. Now its placement is more debatable, but it's […]
articles.content:
The new update comes from Nash Weedle , an insider known for scoops pertaining to Nintendo, who, among other things, was one of the first to relay word of the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Recent reports , including from the reliable Nate the Hate , have suggested that a remake of Majora's Mask is not only not in the works, but not in the immediate plans of Nintendo. Nash Weedle's new update seems to suggest otherwise.

According to Nash Weedle, translated by Hugo Gaming , the remake is real, or at least he believes it is, based on one single piece of information provided to him. He does not disclose what this piece of information is, though.

“I’ve received some information about this supposed remake,” said Nash Weedle. “For now, I can only tell you that I’m looking into it. But I assure you that this one piece of information alone has made me believe that the Majora’s Mask remake is real.”

Let's take this new report at face value and also assume that development on The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask Remake has already begun or is imminent. It took three years for Nintendo to remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . For various reasons, Majora's Mask should be quicker than this, but at the bare minimum it won't take longer. So, if a remake of Majora's Mask has begun or is about to begin, we are looking at a late 2028 release date at the earliest, but 2029 and 2030 are certainly on the table as well.

The question is when it will begin. The team that would work on it is no doubt going to support Ocarina of Time , but this doesn't take the full team. Meanwhile, the holiday is imminent, so perhaps development will begin at the start of 2027, but this is just speculation. The game needs minimal time in pre-production, considering it's both a remake and going to be in the same style and spirit as the Ocarina of Time Remake , presumably. In other words, less to figure out in pre-production.

At the moment of publishing, Nintendo has not been drawn out for comment. We do not expect this to change, but if it does, we will update the story accordingly.

articles.title: More Evidence Sydney Sweeney Might Be Following In Prince Harry And Meghan Markle’s Footsteps And Planning A Move
articles.summary: Is Sweeney really heading to the UK?
articles.content:
As Sydney Sweeney continues to generate buzz due to her acting career, buzzy lingerie line , those splashy ads and more business ventures, there’s been a continued focus on her personal life. That includes her relationship with Scooter Braun, who has reportedly been helping her make career decisions. As rumors continue to swirl around their relationship, it’s been alleged that Sweeney wants to move to the UK. Now, there’s apparently more evidence that she’s planning a move like Meghan Markle and Prince Harry’s.

Not only has it been alleged that the Euphoria alum is looking for a new residence in the UK, and this claim has sparked a bit of speculation. A recent report from The Sun sheds more light on the purported matter and, according to the outlet, Sweeney recently viewed a property in the village of Little Tew. Per a source, the actress has allegedly informed her people in her inner circle that she’s aiming to split her time between the UK and her multiple properties in the United States. A source for the tabloid also said this:

If Sweeney were to make the move, she would actually become just another one of the famous people who live in the area. Among the celebrities who live in the area are David and Victoria Beckham, Ellen DeGeneres and her wife, Portia de Rossi ( whose house was thought to have flooded in 2024) and Jeremy Clarkson. The Sun’s insider went on to allege that due to the presence of multiple stars, Sweeney wouldn’t have to worry about residents making a fuss over her, and there’s apparently another benefit:

This should all be taken with a grain of salt, considering that no one from Sydney Sweeney’s camp has confirmed or denied that she’s planning to make a new home across the pond. Still, this news comes at an interesting time, considering what’s been going on with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex as of late.

It was reported this past August that Markle and Prince Harry were moving back to the UK alongside their two kids, Archie and Lilibet. For the past six years, the pair lived in Montecito, California, as they relocated to the state after stepping back from roles as senior members of the British Royal Family. Harry and Markle reportedly used a private jet to return to the UK, and the trip allegedly cost them $120,000 in total.

Since returning to the country, the Duke and Duchess’ family has reportedly stayed with friends in the aforementioned Cotswolds. Earlier this month, though, it was reported that the pair had already slightly relocated . Apparently Markle, Harry and their brood moved to the “main house” on the estate after having lived in a “property on the estate.” As for the couple’s attempts to find a place of their own, it’s been alleged that their search has been stalled due to their “champagne tastes” purportedly not matching their financial portfolio.

articles.title: People Said Daniel Radcliffe Was ‘F--ked’ After Harry Potter. How He Succeeded Anyway
articles.summary: The boy who really lived.
articles.content:
The Harry Potter film series may have ended in 2011, but its lead, Daniel Radcliffe , remains a household name. He’s made a splash not only by taking on so many “weird” film projects , but he's also made a mark in TV and on Broadway. If you can believe it, the British actor himself said people told him he would have career troubles after his Wizarding World days. However, Radcliffe ultimately succeeded, and he recently recalled how all that happened..

It's a real shame that people suggested that to Radcliffe and put so much pressure on him at a young age. From the outside looking in, it almost seemed like he was being set up to fail. I can understand that there are many actors out there who are forever remembered for one role . However, that didn't necessarily mean the December Boys actor would be one of them. Radcliffe continued to explain on the podcast that he didn’t let anyone’s negativity bother him:

After Radcliffe spent so many years playing The Boy Who Lived, I can really understand why he'd go down a path of self-discovery. Even his Harry Potter co-star, Alan Rickman , advised him and other alumni to try theater. And lo and behold, Radcliffe would eventually star in the Broadway show Merrily We Roll Along, which made tons of money and landed him his first Tony Award.

Well, there you go. It appears that directors wanted the credit to be able to help show Radcliffe’s versatility outside of playing a wizard. Of course, many filmmakers naturally become impressed when an actor knows how to step outside of his comfort zone and take on different roles. To that point, Radcliffe’s former Harry Potter director, Chris Columbus, was definitely impressed with the talented actor’s career moves when the franchise ended, saying his projects showed how “fearless” he was.

articles.title: Naruto Shadow Rising Drops New Tease for Original Creator's Manga Return
articles.summary: Courtesy of Shueisha Naruto's original creator Masashi Kishimoto is returning to the franchise for a new manga to help expand its timeline, and Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump has dropped a new tease for the creator's big return. Naruto is now in the midst of a massive new endeavor with the intent of releasing new manga, TV anime, video […]
articles.content:
Naruto Shadow Rising was shockingly announced to be in the works earlier this Fall during a worldwide streaming panel at New York Comic Con 2026. Revealed to be a new manga from Masashi Kishimoto himself, not much in the way of concrete information has been confirmed as of this time. But one of the latest issues of Shonen Jump ( as spotted by @Shinuki1992 on X ) has given fans a new tease about Naruto ‘s new manga return.

Naruto: Shadow Rising teaser in the Weekly Shonen Jump Issue #50 of 2026: "Holding up his Hokage hat, Naruto and Sasuke clashes in a fierce battle!!!" More information about the story will be revealed on Jump Festa 2027 in December 19! pic.twitter.com/TksI4AY2PE

Naruto Shadow Rising features Kishimoto returning with a new manga story, but it's yet to be revealed what kind of shape this new story will take. It could be a single one-shot story focusing on a time Naruto and Sasuke fought before Naruto became the Hokage ( something that was not shown during the events of the main series ), or it could be a miniseries with multiple chapters set to release much like other sequels of its kind like Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo . But there are still many other questions surrounding this return that just keep popping up.

Naruto Shadow Rising seems to take place after the original series, but before the events of the Boruto: Naruto Next Generations sequel . It's kind of like Dragon Ball Super' s situation where it can't do too much without interfering with the canon of its future events seen in the sequel, but that franchise has gone on for so long that it's basically become its own timeline. That could be the case with this manga return, or it could end after a single chapter. We'll find out soon enough when it takes the stage during Jump Festa 2027 later this year.

Naruto is one of the many franchises that Shueisha will be showcasing during Jump Festa 2027 over the December 19-20 weekend , and it's been confirmed that fans will get their next major update about Naruto Shadow Rising at the time as well. This will likely help to alleviate some of the questions fans have about it all such as potential release format and schedule, length of its story and more. Either way, it's a big deal as Kishimoto readies for a full comeback to manga after all this time.

Naruto also has many other new projects now in the works for the near future such as a new crossover anime revival together with a Shonen Jump classic, Naruto x Ninku , a new trading card game hitting shelves, a new mobile game title readying for its launch, and even a new live-action feature film heading into production next year. articles.title: VisionQuest Post-Credits Scene Wasn’t the Only Idea the MCU Pitched to Bring Wanda Back
articles.summary: Marvel Studios This article contains spoilers for the VisionQuest season finale. Everyone knows (and hates) that Wanda met her end in the final act of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. But now, years later, the Scarlett Witch is emerging from the rubble—literally. As the credits rolled on VisionQuest, fans were treated to a post-credit scene […]
articles.content:
With VisionQuest having just ended , traumatizing everyone with that post-credits scene, and Avengers: Doomsday on the horizon, there's one thing on everyone's mind: Wanda Maximoff. And it was up to Terry Matalas to bring her back in a way that would solve multiple problems: continuity and closure. “She was the missing component of that finale, and we talked about a dozen different ways to bring her back. This was the one that felt like the biggest promise of more for everybody. It came together really fast, and was really collaborative in a very fun way,” he said when speaking with Gold Derby about her inevitable return.

Originally, Matalas wanted Wanda to appear earlier, but he eventually changed his mind, deciding the end-credits scene was the perfect moment. “We had talked about having her appear in a dreamlike ways, but if that happened at the wrong time, the episode would become about that,” he went on to say. “It really needed to be about Vision, so the end credits sequence was the perfect way to address Wanda.” And he might have been right, at least in terms of Wanda's return overshadowing parts of Vision's journey. One fan said , “The way just seeing her briefly during the ultravision segment when Vision thought of her completely stole the show for me.”

The scene itself came as a surprise even to critics who had early access to the episode. But Marvel made the decision to attach the scene just as it was debuting on Disney+ for its full audience. We don't yet know what this scene means for Wanda's future, whether it be in service to Doom or with her powers drained by him ( potentially leaving her fully human ), but it's safe to say that there is a future for one of Marvel's best characters, even if she won't be a main feature in Doomsday , which is already juggling a wildly unruly number of characters. It is worth noting that she could have a place in the upcoming X-Men saga—especially if Marvel finally uses the connection between her and Magneto as father and daughter.

articles.title: Remake of 1980s Sega Game Now Available on Nintendo Switch for $3.99
articles.summary: A remake of a 1980s Sega game is now available on the Nintendo Switch for $3.99. This is thanks to an exclusive Nintendo eShop sale that is live until November 19. There is notably no Nintendo Switch 2 version of the game; however, the Switch version is playable on the Switch 2 via backward compatibility. […]
articles.content:
Back in 1989, specifically, developer Westone and publisher Sega — the former of which went belly up in 2014 — released Wonder Boy III: The Dragon's Trap as a new installment in the Wonder Boy series. In 2017, this game was remade by developer LizardCube and publisher DotEmu. This remake is called Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap , and it's dirt cheap on the Nintendo eShop right now, as well as everywhere else it is available. This is in addition to a $70 Nintendo Switch game that's been discounted to just $7 .

For those unfamiliar with Wonder Boy III: The Dragon's Trap , it was a Sega Master System exclusive game when it initially came out, though it ended up coming to other platforms, including the Game Gear, PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16, and mobile devices. And this 37-year-old game does not hold up very well unless you have the Sega Master System nostalgia that goes along with it. That's what the remake has, because it plays as well in 2026 as it did in 2017. To this end, if you were going to remake it in 2026, it would probably be nearly identical to what LizardCube produced in 2017.

One of 2017's Most Underrated Games When Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap was released in 2017, it earned an 80 on Metacritic, a very solid score. And this more or less lines up with its user reviews across the Internet. The Nintendo eShop doesn't have user reviews, but on Steam, for example, it has an 86% approval rating.

As for the game itself, it is a platform adventure game that takes about 5 to 8 hours to beat, depending on a handful of variables. So, it's not terribly content-stuffed, which is a deal-breaker for some, but a non-issue when the game only costs $4. Meanwhile, considering this is the cheapest the game has ever been in 9 years, it is hard to imagine it getting much cheaper than this anytime soon.

If $4 is too much for your wallet right now, there are some other cheaper options available. To this end, three free upgrades for three Nintendo Switch games were just released .

articles.title: Oprah Just Found Out People NOT Named Tom Cruise Can Actually Order The Tom Cruise Christmas Cake
articles.summary: My mouth is already watering!
articles.content:
For a number of families, the Christmas Season is all about Santa Claus and his gift-giving, but in Hollywood, Santa comes in the shape of Tom Cruise and his famous Christmas cake. Even Oprah Winfrey spends the holiday season waiting around for the legendary coconut cake to arrive on her doorstep. However, that seems to be changing this year now that Oprah has discovered the cake isn’t as exclusive as she thought.

Now, I don’t think anyone thought Cruise was baking the Christmas coconut cakes himself. While he’s a talented actor and impressive stuntman , baking is time-consuming, and his schedule is usually packed. The identity of the bakery that prepares the cakes isn't a total secret, but now, Oprah has let that cat out of the bag on a grand scale.

The Emmy-Award-winning host rejoiced at being able to order the cake whenever she wants. And in true Oprah fashion, her first instinct was to share the good news with those in her life:

I'm wondering how Cruise will feel knowing that Winfrey has further emphasized the source of his famous gift With this, might he consider changing up his yuletide tradition and switch to something? It's hard to say, but even if he did, I'm sure he'd think of something just as special. After all, the Mission Impossible star is known for his generosity, like never forgetting to call Rosie O’Donnell for her birthday.

I would be insanely jealous, but of course, the good news is that anyone can order the cake from Goldbelly right now. It’s not exactly cheap, but it might be worth it to say that I’ve tried the infamous “ Tom Cruise Cake,” thanks to Oprah.

articles.title: South Park Finally Gives Tweek x Craig Their Own Episode After 9 Years
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of South Park Studios South Park Season 29 has made major waves with fans over its episodes thus far, but the latest has gotten some of the best responses yet as Tweek and Craig have their first focus episode in nearly ten years. South Park has been making adjustments after everything that happened with Seasons 27 and 28 last […]
articles.content:
South Park Season 29's “We Be Clubbin'” sees the series shifting further away from any of its overt political commentary following the United States midterm elections ( as evident by PC Principal's retcon upon his return ), and with it hilariously also addresses a major fan complaint with its last episode. After revealing that they “forgot” Tweek and Craig's anniversary, the episode itself is the first focus story for the duo in nine long years as they get some very real development.

South Park Season 29 Episode 5's “We Be Clubbin ‘” sees Craig get very involved in club sports. Cartman and the rest of the school realize that while they have been focusing on so many other things, Tweek and Craig's anniversary had slipped by. It turned out this was the same case for Craig as he also forgot and thus it leads to Tweek getting involved with club sports to get closer to him. But this hilariously seems like a response to some of the fan complaints that had popped up online this past month. Which usually isn't South Park ‘s style.

October 28th was the 11th anniversary of the classic Season 19 episode, “Tweek x Craig,” where Tweek and Craig were forced into a relationship together thanks to the fact that girls around town had drawn a lot of art shipping the two together. Their relationship has stayed firm for all these years since, but they rarely have had a focus on that actual dynamic. The last episode that focused on them came during Season 21's “Put it Down” back in 2017. So this was a welcome return for the duo for those heavily invested fans who wanted to see more of them.

With the 11th anniversary going by and South Park choosing to instead focus on other things, supporters of the Tweek x Craig relationship had been very vocal online about the episodes instead introducing characters like Little Randy . Seemingly as a way to both poke fun at the contingent of these fans and genuinely address the idea, the episode has Cartman openly apologize to the duo for forgetting about the anniversary. Then it makes the entire episode about that fact.

South Park has had a history of directly addressing fans and critics in the episodes themselves , but this is one of the few examples where they seemingly catered to a contingent of fans online. It ended up in a fun episode as a result, so maybe they might do more of this in the future. But then again, it won't be long before South Park pokes fun at the rest of the world especially with its finale coming soon.

articles.title: I Just Found Out Why Johnny Galecki’s Returned To Acting After Years Away
articles.summary: The actor expained his long break.
articles.content:
For years, Johnny Galecki was one of network television's biggest stars. His long-running sitcom, The Big Bang Theory was a hit, and hits bring fame and big paydays. Galecki could have taken his money and retired to a quiet life, and it turns out he wrestled with that decision between then and his latest gig as I just found out.

Galecki did indeed have options considering how much money he made from The Big Bang Theory . He reportedly makes a good deal more via reruns as well , so it's not like he needed to return to acting. And yet, as someone who has been working as an actor since childhood, it was a major part of his identity. Taking on this role was a test to see if he still loved being a performer, or if he needed to figure out what the next chapter of his life looked like.

It's interesting to read that comment, and I do wonder if that's meant to be a pointed jab at what roles could've been waiting for him. It's easy to imagine that Stuart Fails to Save the Universe would love to bring in Johnny Galecki to reprise Leonard Hofstadter eventually, likely for one of the cameo roles we've seen others like Kaley Cuoco play . Is this a hint that co-creator Chuck Lorre shouldn't hold his breath about the Leonard actor reprising the role?

The release caps a major run for "KPop Demon Hunters," which became one of Netflix's biggest original film breakouts after releasing last June. Directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and produced in partnership with Sony Pictures Animation, the film follows K-pop superstars Rumi, Mira and Zoey — voiced by Arden Cho, May Hong and Ji-young Yoo — who lead double lives as demon hunters when they aren't selling out stadiums.

The film, which won the Oscar for best animated feature , broke multiple records over the past year. It became the most streamed movie of 2025 while its corresponding soundtrack hit No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The lead single "Golden" remained at No. 1 on the Hot 100, with the film becoming the first soundtrack to place four songs in the chart's top 10 at the same time.

The film has also spawned dozens of lucrative partnerships and licensing deals. In fact, Mattel and Hasbro, fierce rivals, were named a global "co-master" toy licensee for "KPop Demon Hunters — a dual license structure believed to be unprecedented in the industry. Themed products such as Uno, Monopoly, and dolls have begun rolling out this spring.

A sequel is currently in development at Netflix and Sony Pictures Animation, with Kang and Appelhans returning. The just-announced tour, meantime, puts the film's animated K-pop trio Huntr/x in front of live audiences. Dates kick off in June.

articles.title: Metal Sonic's Unleashed in New Sonic Anime Short for 35th Anniversary - Watch Now
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of SEGA / GXS Productions Sonic the Hedgehog has gone all out to celebrate its 35th anniversary, and it's fully unleashed Metal Sonic with a cool new anime style short showing off a very tough fight. Sonic the Hedgehog has become one of the most notable video game icons in its over three decade run, and the video games themselves […]
articles.content:
Sonic the Hedgehog: Memories and Beyond is a special new animated short produced by SEGA for the franchise's 35th anniversary , and it puts Sonic and the rest of his friends in one of their toughest fights yet. With Dr. Eggman unleashing Metal Sonic, fans get to see a whole new level of actions for the favorites that has rarely been seen elsewhere. You can check out the new animated short below to see all of the action.

Sonic the Hedgehog: Memories and Beyond was directed by Kevin Molina-Ortiz for GXS Productions ( the same studio behind the Sonic x Shadow Generations: Dark Beginnings anime ) in collaboration with SEGA with a script provided by Ian Flynn. The voice cast from the original games return to reprise their respective roles with Roger Craig Smith as Sonic, Colleen O’Shaughnessey as Tails, Dave B. Mitchell as Knuckles, Kirk Thornton as Shadow, Cindy Robinson as Amy, Karen Strassman as Rouge, and Mike Pollock as Dr. Eggman. The short's been released in multiple languages too.

If you wanted to see the Japanese language version (which unfortunately does not feature multi-language subtitles), it features a voice cast with Jun-ichi Kanemaru as Sonic, Ryo Hirohashi as Tails, Nobutoshi Canna as Knuckles, Koji Yusa as Shadow, Taeko Kawata as Amy, Rumi Ochiai as Rogue, and Kotaro Nakamura as Dr. Eggman instead. But given Sonic's long history with the world of anime with projects in the past like Sonic X , it's no mystery as to why such high-octane action works in this style. It's been proven to be a success before.

Appropriately so for the speedy icon, Sonic the Hedgehog is showing no signs of slowing down anytime soon. Not only are there always new video game projects now in various stages of development, but the franchise is now in the works on its fourth major live-action film. Sonic the Hedgehog 4 is currently scheduled for a release on March 19th next year , but not much from the film has been officially revealed in motion. That's going to change soon enough as we get closer to 2027, thankfully.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 will be introduced Kristen Bell to the voice cast as the voice of Amy Rose, and it's been confirmed that the new film will be introducing Metal Sonic to the fray too. If the movie can tap into any of the buzz or action seen in this animated short, then it's likely we're in for a good time. How do you feel about this new Sonic the Hedgehog animated short? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

Conservatories, typically built around intensive studio training in performance and composition rather than the broad general education requirements of a traditional college, made a strong showing in THR ‘s annual look at the world's best music schools. But schools with well-regarded media scoring programs, which teach composing for film, TV, video and gaming — USC Thornton, Eastman, Berklee and Columbia Chicago — retain their influence in Hollywood and beyond.

David Serkin Ludwig, dean and director of the music division at Juilliard, which continues to expand its opportunities for media scoring, says that the grounding conservatories give their students is important in a world where AI is encroaching even on creative disciplines like music. “A great hedge against the replacement aspect of AI is having a very deep and thorough training, because you want depth of knowledge and experience for people using the tools,” he says. “So I'm happy with the direction we're going, and we just have to keep staying current.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys' Bass Singer, Dies at 83 Music Meet Plave, the Very Real Virtual K-pop Boy Group

To see where that type of training is happening, we turned to the people working in the field. Contributing to this year's ranked list via survey: the Society of Composers and Lyricists, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences' music branch, the Alliance for Women Film Composers and the Composers Diversity Collective. Thanks go to Ray Costa and Costa Communications for their help in distributing THR ‘s survey.

Long a holdout on media scoring instruction, Juilliard now offers several courses, including Composing for Visual Media, which gives students the fundamental skills they need to compose for film and TV, as well as commercials and video games, with focuses on both traditional and more diverse contemporary approaches. Berklee now also offers a Master of Arts in music supervision, the first of its kind in the world: a one-year, fully online graduate program covering the art of selecting, licensing and integrating music into TV, games and advertising and taught by music supervisor pros like Julia Michels ( The Devil Wears Prada ).

Undergraduate programs include a four-year bachelor of music degree that offers studio performance training and courses on musical theory, music history, ear training and the humanities, with students completing both junior and senior solo recitals. The Performance Diploma is a four-year nondegree program for students with ambitions of professional performance but who do not yet have a bachelor's degree. Yale offers a master of music, master of musical arts, doctor of musical arts and artist diploma in composition, with courses taught by concert hall composers including Katherine Balch, Martin Bresnick and Aaron Jay Kernis. While the school does not offer degree programs in media scoring, Yale's Center for Collaborative Arts and Media helps students combine music with film, video, computer science and the visual arts. articles.summary: The hierarchy of power in the DC Universe has changed once again, and this time it's not The Rock trying to make Black Adam more relevant than he is. articles.content:
Unlike the calm, measured, and ‘fearless' version we saw in the show, the 1960 comic portrays John Stewart with a more brash and rugged persona. Right from the cover, you can see Stewart standing in a defiant manner, holding up a defeated Hal Jordan, with the words “Beware my power” from the Green Lantern oath highlighted. Even in the panels, Jordan first finds him standing up against a crooked cop for the right reasons. Despite his doubts, the Guardians reassure Jordan that he's the right choice for a new recruit. He quickly learns that Stewart has his own way of doing things, which may not exactly line up with Jordan's proper approach. If anything, the HBO show swapped the dynamic between the two from this issue.

For those of us growing up in the late '90s and early 2000s, John Stewart was the original Green Lantern. This was primarily down to the Justice League animated series featuring him as the primary Lantern on the roster. Since it was the most popular DC property of its time, a lot of us weren't even aware that Hal Jordan was technically the main Green Lantern in the DC Universe. That's just another reason why this comic is so valuable, especially to millennials who grew up with Stewart as their Lantern. Aside from that, its high grade and the fact that it has off-white to white pages has further boosted its overall value. The second appearance of Guy Gardner may have added on a few dollars as well.

With this new shakeup at DC, only time will tell if we'll get a second season of Lanterns , or if the hierarchy decides to take another route. We know that Aaron Stone Pierre was set to reprise his role as John Stewart in Man of Tomorrow , which will still go ahead as planned, but perhaps his role might get edited out to pave the path for a new approach. Regardless of what eventually happens, this milestone issue will always be remembered for giving us millennials the Green Lantern we grew up with. It may be a while before we see another Green Lantern movie or TV show, but this issue will always remain coveted among fans and comic book collectors.

articles.title: Alvin & The Chipmunks Just Made Their AI Controversy Much Worse Ahead of New Movie
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Bagdasarian Productions Alvin and the Chipmunks has been caught in a whole new AI controversy as fans are alleging a new video has been fully AI generated, and it's only made things more questionable for the future of the franchise. Alvin and the Chipmunks has been caught in a wave of all sorts of changes and controversies […]
articles.content:
Alvin and the Chipmunks revealed earlier this year that it was now working on a new franchise reboot feature film, and has been mired in one backlash after another as fans have been against it from the very beginning. Even though the production has since spoken out against the AI allegations against the new film, a new children's song video shared on the franchise's official YouTube has sparked this AI controversy all over again. Check out the video in question below.

The new “Lil' Alvin and the Chipmunks” video released featuring their rendition of “Wheels on the Bus!” on the franchise's official YouTube channel has sparked AI allegations from fans. Even dedicated fan accounts on social media such as @chipmunk_mania on X have gone as far from asking other fans to avoid supporting the video entirely, “There are so many talented creators in this fandom who deserve your viewership much more than this AI slop.” But unfortunately this is yet another major AI controversy in such a short time.

When Alvin and the Chipmunks first announced a new reboot movie was in the works, a seemingly new design for Alvin made its way online. This resulted in a huge backlash from fans as they noticed it was AI generated , and it led to the film's production needing to address the controversy and note that it was not Alvin's actual design. But no official first looks have been revealed from the new reboot yet. And that's only getting worse with the release of official music videos like this that bring up that fear again.

Alvin and the Chipmunks has yet to fully reveal what the new reboot film is going to look like when it's in motion, but there's likely not going to be much AI generated artwork in it after such a huge backlash from the fanbase . This new reboot has yet to confirm a release date or window as of this time, but it's reportedly going to make its debut in 2028. But there are also multiple routes it can take when it hits as the franchise has a storied history with both fully animated and live-action/CG hybrid releases. The latter films might even be the most popular version of the franchise after all these years.

Former Paramount Co-Chief Executive Brian Robbins’ Big Shot Pictures announced development on a new Alvin and the Chipmunks reboot after investing in a 25% stake in the franchise together with producers Janice Karmen and Ross Bagdasarian Jr of the original owner company, Bagdasarian Productions. The two of them have noted how involved with everything in the new version they are as it could be a new origin story, but very little has been fully set in place as of this time.

articles.title: Chris Evans' Forgotten Superhero Movie Is an Underrated Gem, And Predates the MCU's Captain America
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Summit Entertainment Chris Evans has been in a lot of superhero movies over his career, and even more comic book adaptations. While almost everyone knows him as Captain America in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), that is because it was the role he played in the most movies. However, it wasn't his first superhero movie or his […]
articles.content:
One movie that remains highly underrated was an original superhero release called Push . In this movie, Evans played a man with superhuman powers who was being hunted by government forces that wanted to weaponize people like him. It had very similar themes to the X-Men franchise and ended up getting a comic book adaptation that spun off from the movie instead of the other way around.

Push is a take on the superhero genre where people are born with superhuman powers and the governments around the world want to either turn them into soldiers or kill them to keep them from becoming threats. Chris Evans plays Nick Gant, an untrained superhuman with telekinetic powers (a Mover). He has been on the run since he watched his father get killed by a government agent named Henry Carver (Djimon Hounsou). Carver has telepathic powers and can control other people (a Pusher).

Before Nick's dad died, he told his son that he would have to help a young girl who gives him a flower in the future, and this finally happens 10 years later when he meets a young girl named Cassie, a 13-year-old Watcher with the power to see into the future. He agrees to help Cassie save a Pusher named Kira, whom Carver is trying to capture to use as the government's latest weapon. The other powers in the movie are Shifters (who can create illusions), Stitches (healers), Shadows (shielding psychics), Sniffs (trackers), Wipers (psychics who can erase memories), and Bleeders (who can emit sonic vibrations and are often used as assassins).

The movie had plenty of twists and turns, and in the end it set up a sequel, although one never came. It also opened up a huge world that was explored in WildStorm's comic book prequel series, bringing Push into the DC-adjacent universe, as WildStorm is an imprint of DC Comics.

Push set up the story for a sequel, including the idea that Nick could help Cassie save her mother and take the battle to the government agencies, using their powers as weapons. But there were a lot of things working against the movie becoming a franchise. The film was a box office failure, making only $49 million worldwide on a budget of $38 million. Since it only made $32 million domestically, it didn't make nearly enough money to make a sequel worth pursuing. Push also had poor reviews , earning a 23% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and a 42% audience score, with complaints that it was overly convoluted.

The movie attempted giant world-building with the hopes that it could warrant a franchise that could open up different parts of the world. However, by throwing so much information into the first movie, it just proved to be a little too much considering it was an original idea, and many viewers just seemed lost and confused by the end. There was one other big reason the movie didn't end up moving on as a franchise.

Two years after Push , Chris Evans joined the MCU in Captain America: The First Avenger . He was the lead in Push , and while the franchise could have moved on without him, there was little chance he would return after his MCU debut made him one of the world's biggest stars. After The First Avenger , he jumped into the Avengers movies and then his own franchise before ending up as one of the catalysts behind Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame . With Evans back for Avengers: Doomsday , there is always a good reason to go back and watch Push, to see Evans' earlier superhero role in a new light.

What are your thoughts on Push ? Let us know your favorite Chris Evans superhero performances in the comments below.

articles.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong's DLC Wait Might Be a Long One, But Not As Long as 4 Other Infamous Expansions
articles.summary: Courtesy of Team Cherry The Sea of Sorrow expansion for Hollow Knight: Silksong was intended to release back in August of this year, but a few months later, the DLC has still not arrived for the celebrated Metroidvania. This heavily reflects the release of the base game, which was mired in mystery and delays until its sudden launch back […]
articles.content:
A Bloomberg interview with Team Cherry, the developers behind Hollow Knight: Silksong , confirmed initial plans to release the Sea of Sorrow expansion before August 21, 2026, but clearly, that hasn't happened yet. Similarly, the “final” DLC for the game had a planned August 2027 window, but delays to Sea of Sorrow may prevent that date from coming to fruition as well. Fans are currently worried about another long cycle of waiting for more Hollow Knight , with minimal updates putting the project in limbo for an unclear amount of time. Ironically, this wait has been short so far compared to others.

The Delicious Last Course is a wonderful expansion to Cuphead , containing new levels, bosses, and even a new character for players to control in the form of Ms. Chalice. What sets this DLC apart from other games is that it not only matches the high-quality of the original game, but often surpasses it in visual presentation. Cuphead is a game that mimics the rubberhose, cartoonish art style of old Disney and Popeye animations, using hand-drawn frame-by-frame artwork to create complex levels for players to experience.

Even the making of Cuphead took forever due to the individual hand-drawn frame approach of the base game, but the expansion was on a whole other level. The Delicious Last Course was announced only one year after Cuphead came out in 2018, yet it took four years to eventually release in 2022. The wait was more than worth it in the end, with the final boss of the DLC being one of the most impressive displays of artistic skill any game has any claim to having. Studio MDHR, the developers of Cuphead , were never deterred by the DLC's delay, prioritizing high standards over something done quickly with half the effort.

In truth, the DLC almost took five years to come out rather than four, as production on it was already underway when the base game of Cuphead dropped. Some players have criticized the short length of the Delicious Last Course , as it only takes around 2-3 hours to beat, but the difficulty of Cuphead adds replayability for those looking to get perfect scores in DLC levels and boss fights. Most fans consider the avoidance of crunch from Studio MDHR to be for the greater good, but not every game with a big delay had this luxury.

The development history of Final Fantasy 15 is, to put it lightly, complicated. The base game took almost 10 years to create, falling into multiple periods of “development hell” due to rebranding of the series and other technical problems, such as switching to a new game engine. Publisher Square Enix had significant changes of leadership too, leading to a doubling down on the MMO formula of Final Fantasy 14 (which worked out for that game in the long run). So, by the time Final Fantasy 15 came out, it was incredibly rushed, with mixed reviews and strange gameplay systems that didn't always fit well together in the final product.

That being said, the Episode Ardyn DLC didn't fair any better, taking around three years after the base game release to come out. This was part of a post-launch plan for Final Fantasy 15 , where new story content was added to build off the game's main characters, with expansion “Episodes” for figures like Gladiolus, Prompto, and Ignis, the companions of protagonist Noctis. By the time Episode Ardyn came out, the DLC was focused on the game's antagonist, providing the final expansion of the game's story before the series would move on. By 2019 when this DLC came out, though, players were far more ready for Final Fantasy 7 Remake to come out the following year.

Anyone who was a fan of Kingdoms of Amalur back in 2012 can tell you that the game was far from perfect, with RPG gameplay that didn't go over quite so well upon its launch. However, the promise of fixes never truly took place, not until the game re-launched itself in 2020 with Kingdoms of Amalur: Re-Reckoning . This was a huge overhaul of the title, not only making it available on modern platforms, but also improving gameplay ideas and refining what was unique about the title. As such, this newfound support allowed players to anticipate new content, in the form of the Fatesworn expansion .

Fatesworn was something that had to be built from the ground-up, as the remastered and refined game had tons of problems developers needed to correct. The final version of the game with the DLC is excellent, but it took until 2022 for players to get their hands on Fatesworn . This marked a ten year gap between the launch version of Kingdoms of Amalur and what can be considered its “definitive” edition. While the Fatesworn edition came with prior DLC content called The Legend of Dead Kel and Teeth of Naros , the third expansion is where the game really came into its own.

To this day, what happened to Kingdoms of Amalur represents one of, if not the, longest gap between a base game and its most anticipated DLC. What made Fatesworn such a major addition to the game was how it finally delivered on a promise from long ago — creating excellent post-game content for players to explore. New mechanics combined with a fresh story and never-before-seen map region, almost feeling like a fresh game drop. Increases to character level caps and expanded crafting, combat, and story features all helped this game survive its long expansion wait time strongly.

The 2014 edition of Mario Kart 8 is something almost unrecognizable today due to its Deluxe expansion, which became a definitive version of the game similar to Kingdoms of Amalur: Re-Reckoning . Originally released for the Wii U, Mario Kart 8 was far from disappointing at launch, as it provided the same arcade racing that fans desired within a new entry to the celebrated series. That being said, fans quickly realized that despite the solid new racing maps and expanded gameplay ideas of Mario Kart 8 , it getting DLC support was going to be a test of patience.

The Deluxe Course Pass DLC for Mario Kart 8 didn't come out until February 2022, a remarkable eight years since the base game came out. At the point of the DLC, most players had moved on to the next Nintendo console, moving from the Wii U to the Switch a long time ago. Fans were expecting a new installment in the series at that point before more tracks, but the surprising expansion was welcomed by those who enjoyed what Mario Kart 8 had developed into on its own. Six sets of eight new racing maps certainly helped this DLC shine, with it acting as a precursor to 2025's Mario Kart World on the Switch 2.

These days, it's more likely that a gaming DLC project will get cancelled rather than release after so much time in limbo like the expansions on this List. Unique cases like indie game DLC has a better chance at survival over time, as they have the excuse of a smaller studio working with limited resources, thus making whatever comes out take longer to create. Hopefully, Hollow Knight: Silksong ‘s Sea of Sorrow expansion doesn't take another eight years to release, but fans should count themselves lucky that a longer delay isn't as likely.

What is your least favorite wait you've ever had to do for a game to come out? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: 5 Marvel Heroes Who Got Costume Redesigns They Definitely Didn't Need
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Superheroes live and die based on their designs. Iconic, bombastic costumes that call upon modern fashion trends and classic circus outfits create a unique look that has cemented countless heroes in the mind's eye. Beloved as they are, most heroes go through redesigns every few years to keep their looks fresh and relevant, and while […]
articles.content:
When Magneto ripped out Wolverine's adamantium in “Fatal Attractions,” it revealed that the yellow-clad hero had bone claws underneath. However, what started as an interesting reveal quickly became a nightmare as Wolverine seemingly devolved into a more animalistic appearance. Apparently, the adamantium was holding back his mutation, which aimed to turn him into a feral beast. The validity of that aside, just looking at this Wolverine is almost disturbing. He looks like a caveman who needs to shave, between his widened face and thick, fur-like hair. Also, why did his nose flatten so much that it practically disappeared? His mutation literally enhances his sense of smell.

Wolverine's new look did not look good because it emphasized the least interesting parts of him while throwing away the parts that fans actually loved. Yes, Wolverine's rage and animalistic tendencies are core tenets of his character, but so are his compact, yellow-clad form and simple look. There's both too much going on and not nearly enough human elements. Wolverine's feral design is the peak of what '90s redesigns aimed to do, making everything far too edgy and sharp to the point of ridiculousness. Wolverine has two iconic looks that are both near-equally accepted by fans, and ditching them for something that destroys his mental image was definitely a mistake.

The Fantastic Four wear simple but clean costumes that have nearly endless room for small adjustments and creative redesigns that maintain the spirit of the original, but this is definitely not one of those cases. Superheroines have always had it rough with costumes, with the vast majority being magnitudes more revealing than their male counterparts, and this is easily Sue's most egregious example, especially considering how she never struggled with this issue before. And oh boy, is this suit the perfect example of that. Seriously, there's almost nothing here. A ton of superheroines' costumes could be called swimsuits, but this skips straight to being lingerie.

Why on Earth is the 4-symbol cut out? Why are there arm bands that connect to nothing? This suit really takes after Sue, given that half of it is just straight up see-through. The in-universe reasoning for this design is that she melded with her sentient Malice persona, which was birthed from all of her darkest thoughts and desires, but still, that just feels like a lame excuse to put Sue on display. Fan sentiment seems to have agreed the entire time, given that this suit was quickly replaced and Sue returned to her normal personality.

Beast didn't used to be a big blue fuzzball , as he initially started out as just being bigger than the average person, complete with a brick-wall-style physique. Of course, after his experiments awakened this side of him, it stuck and became a core trait, but he was actually once reverted to his original, human look. It occurred during the original X-Factor (1986) run, which wanted to restore the original five X-Men in every capacity, and that included returning Beast to his original design. Frankly, it's baffling, given just how much being blue and monstrous-looking adds to his character and his place in the mutant metaphor.

Beast actually looking like a beast makes him ten times more interesting than looking like a bulky man. What was even weirder is that this change was followed by a decrease in his intellect, where he traded his smarts for raw power. That was clearly a band-aid to restore some of the internal drama that was lost when he was made to look normal again, but it just took away another essential character trait in a convoluted way to restore what this design change took away. Beast's human design isn't bad, but it definitely made him a worse character.

Daredevil's red costume is one of the simplest and most beloved designs in Marvel, which makes any changes to it especially difficult and subject to ridicule. There have been good redesigns, such as the All-New, All-Different black version, but the armor is not that. In fact, it's probably the look everyone points to first when talking about terrible redesigns. Simply put, there's way too much going on here. There's both too much red and not nearly enough, with the bits that are there sticking out like sore thumbs, given that they're genuine armor instead of the spandex or cloth that it normally is. The steel bits stick out even harder. Why does Daredevil have forearm spikes, and why can he attach his billy clubs to them?

When people think of Daredevil, they think of acrobatics and ninja adventures . He's a quick fighter who uses stealth as much as he does his fists, and yet this costume has him lumbering around in armor that wouldn't look out of place on a modern knight. That's not even getting into how it's just not pleasing to look at. The small DD logo looks like it's printed on in the worst way, and the chest plate juts out in the strangest way to make him look unbalanced. This is Daredevil's worst look by far, and it's no mistake that the most recent time it was brought back in Daredevil (2023) #20, it was used as a bondage joke.

“Avengers: Armageddon” was a massive shakeup for the Marvel Universe , with Red Hulk's detonation turning the world against superheroes. Captain Marvel was literally at ground zero, and the radiation she absorbed left her depowered and traumatized. That's the explanation for her new look, but that does not make the pill any easier to swallow. The first change was giving Carol the pixie cut again, which isn't going to work for her specifically no matter how many times Marvel tries it. That's the least of the problems here, as Carol now sports the top half of her costume and jeans instead of the lower half. Genuinely, this makes her look like she's wearing a Captain Marvel T-shirt.

This new look does not work. It's meant to show that the Avengers have transitioned to being a more grounded team and how much of a low point Captain Marvel has hit, but this is still a bad superhero design, and it's made even worse by the fact that her previous costume was her best look yet. The jacket and braid combo elevated her look so much and screamed superhero, mixing fashion with classic costume extravagance. Knowing that we lost that design to this one hurts in a way that's bound to stick around for some time, as we fell from the greatest heights to the depths of jeans on superhero costumes.

Which Marvel hero do you think should never be redesigned, and which character desperately needs one? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Suikoden: The Anime is an official TV anime adaptation of Konami's classic video game franchise, and the original role-playing games are still held in high regard by fans all these years. Although they had been previously available with the series' official YouTube channel since it premiered earlier this October, Crunchyroll is now streaming the series ‘ first six episodes and will be a home for its future episodes releasing on a weekly basis from here on out.

The first six episodes of Suikoden: The Anime are now streaming with Crunchyroll for fans in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Central America, and South America with English and Spanish subtitles (with Portuguese subtitles being available on November 17th). New episodes will be released on a weekly basis on Tuesdays at 6:30AM PT beginning with Episode 7 on November 17th, so fans will be able to catch up just in time for the weekly releases of the future episodes to come.

Originally making its debut earlier this October , Suikoden: The Anime is an adaptation of Konami's original Suikoden II game. YUZO is directing the new anime for KONAMI animation with Michihiro Tsuchiya handling the scripts, Ryo Yamauchi provides the character designs (with Fumi Ishikawa credited for the original game), Koji Nakamura composing the music, and Ryo Hino producing on behalf of NBCUniversal Entertainment Japan. But now that it's come to Crunchyroll, fans of the original games will be able to jump into the new series as it hits.

Suikoden: The Anime features a voice cast including the likes of Toshiki Kumagai as Riliu, Shimba Tsuchiya as Jowy, Ayumi Hinohara as Nanami, Katsuyuki Konishi as Viktor, Yuichi Nakamura as Flik, Taku Yashiro as Luca Blight, Chika Anzai as Jillia Blight, Akihiro Mine as Rowd, Tsukino Chikasada as Pilika, Ayumu Murase as Luc, Takeo Otsuka as Shu, Yoshino Aoyama as Apple, Masato Niwa as Mukumuku, Jun Kasama as Culgan, Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Seed, Megumi Han as Leknaat, Shota Hayama as Gengen, Ryunosuke Watanuki as Rikimaru, Saya Hitomi as Rina, and more.

For those who loved the original game that the anime is based on, thankfully Suikoden: The Anime doesn't deviate too far from that game's original story for its interpretation of it. Set in a period of temporary peace between two warring countries, it seems there are going to be other mysterious plans in place to enact war once more. And only the hero can stop it before it happens. Are you going to check out Suikoden: The Anime on Crunchyroll? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

Following the release of Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ debut season it was confirmed that the series has been renewed for Seasons 3 and 4 . That means there won't be that long of a wait in between each season, so fans will be able to jump into the future sooner than expected.

As detailed by Paramount+, Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 will be kicking off its 13 episode run with the streaming service beginning on May 21st next year. This sets up a likely Fall 2027 release for the third season of the series, and that will give fans quite a lot of the animated series to work through next year.

It makes a lot of sense to see such a quick release schedule for Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ future seasons as showrunner Sehaj Sethi told ComicBook ahead of the release of the first season that the team was already in the works on Seasons 3 and 4 . The entire production of the series has been going on for three years at this point, so it seems like Paramount+ and Avatar Studios has been hard at work all this time to make sure the animated series could have such a stacked release when it finally made its premiere. And that's going to be able to capitalize on any fan fervor.

Avatar: Seven Havens will be running for four seasons in total as teased by the producers behind it all, and it has been making great strides compared to its The Legend of Korra predecessor . The team has worked out its story from the very beginning rather than extending it with new seasons as it goes on, so fans just need to wait to see what's next for Pavi and Nisha moving forward. articles.title: I Rewatched Jackie Chan's Rumble In The Bronx And We Forget Why This Is Such A Gem
articles.summary: "Come on, Jackie Chan.Uh uh uh uh uh oh!"
articles.content:
I love Jackie Chan. You love Jackie Chan. We ALL love Jackie Chan. However, I think we sometimes forget when we started loving Jackie Chan.

As a Black dude, I love martial arts movies (honestly, who DOESN’T?). The thing is, I’m usually into SERIOUS martial arts films, like stuff from the Shaw Brothers, JCVD classics like Time Cop , and old Bruce Lee joints . Then, in 1995, a movie came along that had everything I love about martial arts, but it was also funny as hell.

I first watched Rumble in the Bronx when I was just a kid, and I seriously hated the villains back then. Well, I'm 43 now, and I STILL hate the villains, which is a true testament to just how awful they are to poor Keung in this film. Yes, the late Marc Akerstream as Tony is the main antagonist, and he's a pretty good villain, but even better is his underling, Angelo, played by stuntman Garvin Cross.

Lastly, can I just talk about how great the stunt work is in this film? It's not the craziest stuff in the world (we would see WAY crazier stuff from Chan in earlier films of his, many of which came stateside following the success of RitB), but when I saw his death-defying stunts in RitB - like a huge jump between buildings! - I was hooked.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time Remake's First Mods Are Already Here, & One Adds Co-Op Multiplayer
articles.summary: Courtesy of Nintendo The recent release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been wildly successful, with the game garnering extremely positive reviews from nostalgic fans and completely new audiences. As such, the game has already gotten tons of support on the Switch 2, with fans already putting together mod projects a little over a […]
articles.content:
Mods for the original Ocarina of Time are some of the most infamous in gaming, turning the classic masterpiece into something new long before a complete remake. Some famous mods include “The Sealed Palace” or “The Missing Link,” which added new stories to Ocarina of Time comparable to an official release by Nintendo themselves. Alternatively, speedrunner hacks and other exploits in Ocarina of Time have long been at the center of that game's community, so it's no wonder that game-altering mods are beginning to appear within the Switch 2 version.

Created by Reddit user u/daurosk , the multiplayer Ocarina of Time remake mod is an open source fan project meant to allow 2-4 players to join up together for playthroughs of the game. The project is in its early stages, with the user looking for others to help advance its development, but even at the basic level, this is still an impressive expansion of what the iconic game normally allows. Currently, the mod has some issues with syncing players together, but it has been released for general audiences to try. For right now, here are some features players can look forward to in the mod:

This mod is designed to be run not off the Switch 2 version of the Ocarina of Time remake, but rather a PC emulation players have to set up themselves. Unlike some other modding projects, players can't just download Ocarina of Time with the mod installed, they have to get the game first and then acquire the mod separately. In the future, there may be packaging the mod with the game files, but due to the recency of the mod, optimization like that could still be somewhat far off.

Yet, once you're able to put everything together, this is one of the most interesting ways to try the remake, showing an innovative path for The Legend of Zelda the series likely won't adopt in mainline titles. Other games like The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom have also arrived onto PC recently through fan projects, alongside Wind Waker and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . However, the overwhelming appeal of Ocarina of Time helped it get modded onto PC the same day it launched on the Switch 2, making this multiplayer mod's rapid arrival not too surprising in the long run.

The co-op gameplay of Ocarina of Time ‘s first major mod for the remake is extensive, giving players ways to explore dungeons, travel the open-world, and defeat enemies together. That being said, there are several glitches and pitfalls of the mod right now, namely among the extra features Ocarina of Time has outside its normal game loop. For example, players can't go fishing together, removing one of the most popular mini-games within the title from co-op compatibility. This is a shame, as fishing seems like the one activity besides “normal” gameplay you would want to do with friends often.

Likewise, players aren't able to play certain Ocarina tunes in the multiplayer mod, at least with sound. All of the mechanical uses for Ocarina songs still work within the context of the remake's gameplay, but the audio sometimes cuts out entirely. This means no Ocarina jam sessions with a band of players in Ocarina of Time , at least until the mod gets past its beta phase. Despite these limitations, the mod is fairly comprehensive right now, although it does not scale enemies to match new player pool sizes as your group adventures around Hyrule.

The Legend of Zelda community has come far over the years, evolving from the 1998 classic to develop incredible technical know-how to make this mod so fast. At this point, it is unclear if split screen will be added, or if the project was created so fast using AI “vibe-based” coding, which would be disappointing. At least for now, the Ocarina of Time remake is something that can be shared now more than ever before, even the incomplete state of this mod has its imperfections.

articles.title: 4 Great Movies That Break the Rules of the Hero's Journey & Are Even Better For It
articles.summary: Think of a great movie, and maybe the first one that comes to mind follows a story where the main character starts out not really knowing what to do, faces a series of challenges, learns a few lessons along the way, and ends up in a better place than where they started. That's basically the […]
articles.content:
Sometimes, reworking that structure can actually make a feature even better than it would have been if it had followed the usual formula. The movies on this list are great examples of how stepping away from traditional storytelling can make a narrative even more interesting. Warning: Spoilers ahead.

The funniest thing about The Big Lebowski being on this list is that its protagonist is probably the worst possible candidate for a Hero's Journey. Jeffrey Lebowski, or simply The Dude (Jeff Bridges) , has no big ambitions, isn't trying to prove anything to anyone, and, if he has it his way, his biggest concerns would always be bowling and enjoying his White Russians in peace. But everything changes when two criminals break into his home by mistake, confusing him with a millionaire who shares his name, and end up ruining his favorite rug. Annoyed by the whole situation, The Dude decides to track down the man responsible for the mix-up and get some compensation, only to find himself caught up in a mess involving kidnappings and blackmail.

Looking at it that way, it seems like everything is setting the stage for an adventure where he has to learn how to deal with complicated situations. However, that was never the point. The Dude doesn't really learn anything and doesn't become more responsible. In fact, he spends most of the movie just trying to figure out what's going on. In a more conventional story, all these experiences would lead to some kind of change in the character's personality, but The Big Lebowski doesn't feel the need to give him a major character arc. The Dude ends up pretty much where he started because, sometimes, someone who wants nothing more out of life than to be left alone can make for a much more entertaining story than someone trying to save the world, for example.

Even if you haven't watched No Country for Old Men , chances are you've heard of it at least once, whether because of its villain, its performances, or the fact that it won an Oscar . But did you know its structure is actually based on the Hero's Journey? And the best part is how the movie subverts it in an unexpected way. Here, we have Llewelyn Moss (Josh Brolin), who seems to have everything a thriller protagonist needs: he's smart, knows how to defend himself, and manages to escape situations that would probably kill just about anyone else. After finding $2 million at the scene of a drug deal gone wrong, he decides to keep the money, even though he knows someone will come looking for it. That's when Anton Chigurh (Javier Bardem), a hitman, shows up and starts hunting him down .

Throughout the movie, everything seems to be building toward that inevitable showdown between the hero and the villain. But instead, the film kills off its protagonist off-screen, without even giving the audience a chance to see their final confrontation. And things don't get much better with Sheriff Ed Tom Bell (Tommy Lee Jones), who spends most of the time trying to find Moss and stop Chigurh, only to retire without solving the case the way he wanted. In other words, in No Country for Old Men , the structure is there, but the film doesn't follow it all the way through . The main character doesn't defeat the villain, who doesn't even face consequences proportional to his crimes. It's a pretty bold storytelling choice, but one that worked amazingly well .

What about the kind of movie about someone trying to achieve a dream? That's the typical story you'd expect to follow the Hero's Journey, but Inside Llewyn Davis wants nothing to do with that. Set in New York's folk music scene in the '60s, we follow the title character (Oscar Isaac) , a talented musician trying to build a career after the death of his former musical partner. With no money, no place to live, and relying on the kindness of friends to have somewhere to spend the night, he keeps performing at small clubs while looking for an opportunity to get recognized. At some point, Llewyn decides to travel to Chicago in hopes of landing a record deal with a music producer, but the trip leads nowhere, and he ends up back in New York in pretty much the same situation.

The idea here is not to make him the typical underdog who just needs one chance to prove his worth. He really is talented, but he's also a difficult person and keeps pushing away the people who could help him. And unlike what happens in many stories like this, these experiences don't seem to teach him anything, as Llewyn keeps making the same mistakes and expecting different results. Overall, it's a much less optimistic approach because it doesn't meet any expectations and might even leave some people frustrated, but it's a very good one if you look at Inside Llewyn Davis from a realistic perspective. Watching a film about overcoming adversity can be rewarding, but following someone who's trying and just not making it can be relatable and make us reflect on our own relationship with our life goals.

Now imagine a story where the main character hits rock bottom. It couldn't go any other way than the predictable path: after losing everything, they get a chance to start over, recognize their own mistakes, and finally make the right choices, right? But The Wrestler shows that a movie can deny its protagonist that kind of redemption and still be absolutely wonderful. The story revolves around Randy “The Ram” Robinson (Mickey Rourke), a professional wrestler who was quite successful in the '80s but is now past his prime and struggling financially. He eventually agrees to take part in a match, but suffers a heart attack and is then warned by his doctor that if he returns to the ring, he might not survive.

The problem is that Randy doesn't really know how to live outside the world he's spent most of his life in. He has opportunities to improve his relationship with his daughter and build a new life, but wrestling is much more than a job to him. So, when he gets the chance to take part in a rematch against his former rival, he decides to return, even knowing the risks. In a conventional story, this would be the moment when he chooses his family and his future over staying trapped in the past, but The Wrestler shows that a second chance isn't always enough to make someone change. The film's ending leaves his fate uncertain and keeps the story from becoming an inspirational tale, turning the Hero's Journey on its head. But there's something else valuable in that choice too: its humanity.

articles.title: Major Shonen Jump Series Officially Ends After 5 Years With Final Release
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha Another major long running series from Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has now come to an end with the release of its final chapter after five years. The last couple of years have seen many of the longer running series from the end of the 2010s and early 2020s come to their respective ends. This […]
articles.content:
Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch had announced it was going to end with the manga's next major chapter , and now that's indeed confirmed to be the case as Witch Watch has now ended with Chapter 270. The final chapter of the series comes five years after its original debut, and features a time skip that sends Morihito, Nico and all of the others forward as fans get one final look at their wacky lives as a way to say goodbye.

Witch Watch Chapter 270 officially brings Kenta Shinohara's long running manga to an end after a year long final arc that saw Morihito and the others taking on some very tough foes. The final chapter of the series moves ahead seven years, and reveals what happened to everyone after the final battle. The group all decided to stay living together until after graduation, then went their separate ways after a while. Morihito and Nico ended up marrying and having a child together (who is nine months old by the time of the final chapter).

Kanshi took over as Tengu Leader from his father, Keigo went overseas, and Miharu's in grad school. But the wackiness kicks back in as, one after another, the three of them all barge in the house and ask to move back in. Kanshi's broke (due to terrible investments), Keigo's looking for what to do next after being dumped by Nemu, and Miharu wants to form his own company to make a fortune. Morihito has since become a police officer, and Nico wants to star being a witch counselor giving advice full time. It's teased that their child might be magical too despite seemingly not inheriting either of their abilities, but at the end of the day they're all living together again and happily moving forward.

Now that Witch Watch has come to an end after five years, it's going to be replaced by a new series that has already made its debut in the same issue of the magazine. High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku creator Ryo Nakama has returned to Shonen Jump with the start of a brand new series after three years. Titled Jan Is in Danger! , it's looking to be another fun comedy series that taps into the same type of vibes that made Ryo Nakama so popular before.

This is the first of three new titles coming to Shonen Jump over the rest of the month as the final wave of major updates for the year , and that means there are two other titles that are likely going to come to an end. It's one final period of changes, so it's time to see what ends next. How do you feel about Witch Watch ending after five years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.
