articles.title: ‘WTF?’ SNL Fans Don’t Know Whether To Laugh Or Cry At Sketch That Hit Way Too Close To Home
articles.summary: One of the most thoughtful sketches SNL has given us in a long time.
articles.content:
SNL is best known for its irreverent characters and sharp political commentary , but some of the best sketches in the history of the show are ones that make pointed observations about society. Think Mom Jeans or Meet Your Second Wife. We got another one of those bangers last night, and many fans felt so heard they weren’t sure if they could even laugh.

You can watch the all-time banger below…

Normally when SNL drops a sketch on social, all of the top comments are about exactly what you would expect. They’re messages about how it is or isn’t funny. They’re observations about who is good in the sketch and who isn’t good in the sketch. That’s not the case with this one. Instead, a majority of the comments on multiple platforms are about how the commentator either feels seen or feels called out . There are comments with first person stories and comments saying their real life is exactly what the woman in the sketch is going through .

Other popular comments on YouTube included one woman saying she almost had “a stroke from rage” while watching. Several said they were going to use the sketch to have a conversation with their siblings because they felt heard. It was the same pattern on X too. A woman who works as an estate attorney said it’s “not funny” because it’s so accurate to what she sees every day. Others commented saying the part about the siblings who did nothing still getting an inheritance felt especially powerful since that was their real life experience. Others just commented the classic, "WTF?"

articles.title: I Threw On Avengers Endgame: Encore To Grab All The New Doomsday Scene Timestamps
articles.summary: MCU die-hards will want to check these out.
articles.content:
Spoilers for Avengers Endgame: Encore ’s new scenes lie ahead.

Fans should know that the first of these four new scenes begins at the 2:48:50 mark and is an extension of the original film’s closing scene. Many will probably remember that the OG cut of the film ends with Steve Rogers (Captain America) reuniting with his former love, Peggy Carter, and enjoying domestic bliss. The extended scene adds an interesting twist to the proceedings, as after the two share their kiss, there’s a knock at their door. While Steve hides, Peggy answers, and the visitor is revealed to be none other than Loki.

The second new scene starts around 2:53:47 and shifts the focus to Dr. Bruce Banner. At this point, the tormented scientist is held up in an underground military complex following his (Jean Grey-induced) rampage in Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Banner is in the middle of recording a video journal about his circumstances and plan to suppress his gamma radiation. In a shocking turn, Doctor Doom (who remains unseen) appears before Banner and says he’s arrived to collect him. The scene ends with the sound of the Hulk’s roar.

Yes, the TVA (introduced in Loki ) makes it return during the third additional scene – which drops at the 2:56:30 mark – in Endgame: Encore , though it’s not exactly an ideal situation for the characters. Mobius M. Mobius arrives at work, where he meets up with colleagues Ouroboros and Casey. It’s there that they and their colleagues witness countless multiversal incursions in real time, much to their horror. With that, OB declares the multiverse is collapsing.

The very end of OG Endgame ’s closing credits features a series of “ting” sounds, which were – at the time – said to be paying homage to Tony Stark forging the Mark I in Iron Man . In Encore , this starts around the 3:04:30 mark , and there’s a very different reason for it. After the sounds are heard, the screen eventually flashes to some quick shots of Victor von Doom forging his infamous mask.

articles.title: Demon Slayer Gets a Major Future Update For the Next 100 Years (But There's a Catch)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable Aniplex and Sony Entertainment have major plans to keep Demon Slayer relevant for the next 100 years, but there's a huge problem with this plan that can't be ignored. Written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge, the manga began serialization in the Weekly Shonen Jump Magazine in 2016 and reached its conclusion four years later. While […]
articles.content:
The first installment of the Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle trilogy made history after crossing the 100 billion yen milestone worldwide, becoming the first Japanese film ever to do so. The franchise will adapt the rest of the Infinity Castle Arc in two more movies, although there hasn't been any confirmation regarding the adaptation of the Sunrise Countdown Arc. While fans await updates on the second part of the movie , Atsuhiro Iwakami, president of Sony Music Entertainment Japan and chairman of Aniplex, Sony’s anime production company, shares his plans for the future of Demon Slayer.

According to Bloomberg via The Japan Times , Iwakami shared, “With Demon Slayer, it is our intent to make this last 10 or 20, if not 50 to 100 years.” He also adds, “We want to make sure we’re part of creating the type of franchise that can withstand decades.” Iwakami specifically mentions Dragon Ball and One Piece , stories that have survived for decades, long enough for parents and their children to be fans of. Sony has the streaming rights to both of these legendary anime, which is all the more reason why they have similar plans for Demon Slayer .

Long-running franchises such as Dragon Ball and One Piece are often carried by nostalgia and new releases, as they raised entire generations of Shonen fans. These stories are timeless classics, and it's almost a given that fans will always have a soft spot for them. On the other hand, Demon Slayer is way too new compared to them, but it's still one of the most popular Shonen of all time.

Last recorded in July 2025, Demon Slayer has sold over 220 million copies of manga, ranking seventh among the best-selling manga series of all time. The popularity only keeps rising, and it wouldn't be surprising if it surpassed Naruto (250 million copies) and Dragon Ball (260 million copies). However, there's one major drawback with Demon Slayer compared to Shonen classics.

The main reason why these two Shonen classics maintained their global fan base through several decades is that they are rather long-running stories. One Piece is still ongoing, and the anime is more popular than ever thanks to its stunning visuals in recent years. Not to mention that the series has released several non-canon movies over the years, and it also announced its first-ever canon movie, God Valley, this year. The story is in its Final Saga, and it will take at least a few years for it to reach a conclusion. Even after the finale, the expansive world-building and dozens of fan-favorite characters ensure that the series will always keep releasing new content.

The fact that One Piece already has several official spin-offs, written by different authors, is a testament to its lasting legacy. The same can be said about Dragon Ball , which has released manga sequels, several anime series, spin-offs, and movies over the past forty years. Even now, fans are anticipating the anime's return with the Galactic Patrol Saga and the manga's return with Toyotaro taking over the helm.

Compared to them, Demon Slayer is a much shorter story with rarely any spin-offs or non-canon stories. The world-building isn't impressive, and the manga's ending made sure that there isn't any room for the story to expand . Not to mention it's been more than six years since the finale, but Gotouge has no plans for returning with a new spin-off or even another story. With this in mind, it will be difficult for Sony to keep the series relevant for decades if all they have is around 200 chapters of the manga.

Do you wish Demon Slayer had a longer story to explore its world? What would you like to see covered in the next few decades after the anime is concluded? Share your thoughts in the comments!

articles.title: GTA 6 Free Code Giveaways Officially Announced
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has announced a pair of giveaways that will give Grand Theft Auto fans the chance to win free codes for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. The giveaways are happening via Kick and Twitch, so those interested in scoring the new Rockstar Games release for free will need an account with […]
articles.content:
For those with a Kick account interested in a free code for GTA 6 , you will need to score a Kick Sunset Reward case. This is a new campaign running between now and December 7, and allows Kick viewers to earn a reward case every day, though there is no guarantee a case will include a code. In fact, what the odds are in general aren't disclosed, but we know there are only 10,000 codes that will presumably be dripped out all the way until the aforementioned deadline. Meanwhile, to earn a case, users must be signed into Kick and watch any livestream on the app for 180 minutes. This is three hours, but there's nobody enforcing that you actually watch the stream in question. Do this, and you should automatically unlock a case.

Twitch is running something very similar, though its giveaway won't start until the game launches on November 19, and its duration will be shorter as well. To this end, the giveaway is only running until November 30. Right now, finer details have not been divulged, but there are expected to be tens of thousands of codes available, which will be distributed to viewers watching participating channels. What the watch time to qualify is, meanwhile, also not disclosed. It's typically a fairly lengthy watch time, though.

We know Kick's giveaway will be the $100 Ultimate Edition , which comes with exclusive content not available in the $80 version. What Twitch will be giving away, meanwhile, has not been communicated.

Given the demand for GTA 6 , which looks set to be the biggest launch in entertainment history , it's likely going to be very difficult to earn a code through either of these giveaways, but for those without $80 burning a hole in their pocket this month, it's an option and a chance.

Grand Theft Auto VI is poised to finally release on November 19, in just four days, via PS5 and Xbox Series X. And if you don't win one of these giveaways, you will need to fork over at least $80 to play it at launch. Ahead of this launch, Rockstar Games has already released the first update for the game , which will be a required download to play the game.

articles.title: Fable's New Gameplay Trailer Features Combat That's Eerily Similar to One of PlayStation's Biggest Franchises
articles.summary: Courtesy of Playground Games Xbox just released a deep dive video going into new gameplay concepts for Fable, showing off characters and combat systems that will be in the 2027 RPG. While the narrative information was enlightening, the action was also very interesting, as it seemed to mimic combat flow seen in other big AAA titles, especially PlayStation's Norse […]
articles.content:
The 16 minute deep dive for Fable released by Xbox is a small showcase presented by developer Playground Games, who went into heavy detail about the title's gameplay and story . The environment shown off in the deep dive was far different from what the new Fable has shown before, with the extended combat sequence in the gameplay clip provided being a bigger highlight. It's worth noting that the combat shown for Fable within the deep dive was at a point described to be “around half way through the game,” giving players a strong indication for how combat evolves from any simple, foundational parts.

The deep dive shown by Xbox comes two months after a larger combat-focused video for Fable that came out a few months ago. However, unlike that brief footage, the deep dive is at a much later point in Fable ‘s story, showing new features that are likely unlocked as characters progress to that midway point of the narrative. As such, the combat from that trailer is likely more accurate to what Fable ‘s combat is like now, from its third-person melee action to the magic and ranged options that seem to be at the player's disposal.

The action of Fable has a striking number of comparisons to Santa Monica's God of War games, but especially God of War Ragnarok due to how magic and special abilities seem to work. The two games aren't just similar because of them both being rooted in third-person combat, but in how they organize the player's decision making into cooldown based systems and limited ranged options. For example, players in Fable have a list of abilities in the bottom right corner of their screen, indicating a number of skills tied to the RT input. Players can activate one of four abilities, but after using them, they have to recover from a cooldown before being cast again.

This is extremely similar to God of War ‘s Relics, which provided special abilities that also took time to recharge. If the comparison is anything to go by, players will have ways to upgrade or enhance the abilities they have in Fable , mixing and matching certain ones to forge a unique character build. At the same time, the combat shown for Fable indicates that players can stop and aim a ranged weapon, swapping from their melee tool to hit targets far away. However, it appears that players have a limited ammunition count to these shots, mimicking how the Norse God of War games restricted Kratos' ranged options to what his companions Atreus or Freya could do.

The big difference in these games is that Fable ‘s combat seems weightier, slower, and more deliberate, sharing the same pace as other action RPGs like Dragon's Dogma 2 . This isn't a “bad” thing by any means, as it forces players to make careful choices when committing to certain attacks. Yet, having the same limitations as God of War Ragnarok means that the game suffers from the same pitfalls as that AAA title, and any other game that adopted the same strategies when it comes to third-person action.

Other comparisons in Fable extend to how its ability cooldown system also reflects games like Final Fantasy 16 as well as God of War Ragnarok , but the game isn't just a compilation of systems you've already seen. Some of the magical abilities shown for the game so far include magic to create lightning bolts on the ground or generate air underneath foes to lift them helplessly into the air. When combined with different move sets for various weapons, there is some depth in Fable ‘s combat, much like how exploring the combat of other AAA games mentioned reveal their complexities.

Players also seem to have access to parry and dodge mechanics in Fable , though that should be unsurprising if you've followed trends in AAA games with an action component. Everything from Phantom Blade Zero , God of War Laufey , and Onimusha: Way of the Sword have been geared around those fundamentals, which looked to be represented at least in their bare basics in Fable ‘s gameplay. At the same time, players are able to deliver cinematic finishing moves to enemies at low health in Fable , another similarity to games like God of War Ragnarok that can't quite be ignored.

With all these gameplay ideas integrated from other titles, the combat for the latest Xbox RPG seems to be fairly straightforward. The deep dive, though, shows off corrupted red enemies, indicating a diversity of foes that could demand players adapt their combat strategy as the game goes along. Hopefully, Fable doesn't rely completely on what games inspired it, giving players the chance to develop their own play style over time as their adventure reaches the point shown in the Xbox showcase.

What do you think about the new Fable ‘s combat so far? Let us know in the comments below!
